relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Antimigraine mAbs act as direct scavengers of CGRP (galcanezumab, fremanezumab, and eptinezumab) or against the CGRP receptor (erenumab).

relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Antimigraine mAbs act as direct scavengers of CGRP (galcanezumab, fremanezumab, and eptinezumab) or against the CGRP receptor (erenumab).

key_findings: Review: CGRP-targeting mAbs (galcanezumab, fremanezumab, eptinezumab) scavenge CGRP and erenumab targets its receptor, with long half-lives and no blood-brain barrier crossing, highlighting peripheral mechanisms.
Safety concerns include cardiovascular effects, AMY1 receptor interaction and anti-drug autoantibody immunogenicity.
